name: law_firm_software_009_grant_pipeline_risk_dashboard
instruction: Build the grant pipeline risk dashboard for firm leadership, batched under the episode batch code (ops_meta), as of the episode date. The dashboard answers three questions the development office tracks, each over its own live population: which funding opportunities still in play have decision deadlines approaching inside the episode row's opp_window_days, what those opportunities are collectively worth at their maximum award, which required reports are coming due inside the same window without a submitted or accepted submission, and which active awards reach their end date inside the award_end_window_days window. The firm's grant-reporting policy (GRANT-REPORT-01) governs which report and opportunity statuses still count as 'in play'. Push exactly one ops_reports row (report='grant_pipeline_risk', batch_code) carrying those four figures. Then detail every opportunity the first figure counted: one ops_reports row per opportunity (report='grant_pipeline_risk_detail', batch_code) with the opportunity's identity, its deadline, and its max award -- derived from the same counted set, not recomputed with a different window. No other 'grant_pipeline_risk' or 'grant_pipeline_risk_detail' rows for this batch may exist. Do not modify any source collection. Every collection this task doesn't write to must remain untouched.

hazards.mechanism: window edges are inclusive on both ends and move with the episode knobs (opp 25-35d, award-end 50-70d) -- an off-by-one at either boundary shifts the counted set (snapshot-confirmed: the 30-day window boundary splits opportunities with deadlines exactly at the edge).

status semantics differ per collection: opportunities 'awarded'/'declined'/'withdrawn' are out of play, but reports only drop out when submitted or accepted -- treating 'draft' or 'revision_required' reports as done undercounts the risk set (snapshot-confirmed mixed statuses).
stage-2 detail rows must derive from stage-1's counted set; recomputing with a different window silently diverges from the dashboard row and fails the cross-check.

success_criteria.summary: One grant_pipeline_risk row with the four window-driven figures (opportunities at risk, their summed max_award, reports due soon not yet submitted/accepted, awards nearing end) and one detail row per at-risk opportunity, all derived from the episode row's windows and the policy's status semantics; dual-path confirmed.

checks.expect: at-risk count and value agree between Python filter and SQL
dashboard row + detail rows exact vs episode-knob windows and policy statuses

domain_searches.query: grant pipeline deadline risk tracking research office
top_results: Federal Grant Reporting Requirements: A Guide (casrai.org)

uniqueness_searches.query: grant pipeline risk dashboard benchmark task deadline window agent

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Two different windows on two different collections plus a policy-driven status filter, with a detail stage that must reuse the first stage's counted set -- recomputing with a shifted window is the natural failure.
